$comment: KAN-518: the acquisition pin for Butchr's crabcast-facing proofs.
CrabCast does not vendor these proofs. It CHECKS THEM OUT at the ref below,
at CI time, into an untracked directory, and runs them in Butchr's own tree.
Vendoring was measured impossible rather than merely judged untidy: every one
of the ten CI-runnable proofs computes `repoRoot = <scriptDir>/../..` and then
reads `daemon/src/*.ts` and/or `daemon/dist/*.js` out of it. Copied into
`crabcast/scripts/`, all ten resolve repoRoot to a tree that has no `daemon/`
and fail — 10/10, none of them silently. See docs/butchr-proof-import.md for
the measurement and for what this pin does NOT cover.
WHO CONSUMES THIS: KAN-519, which wires the CI job. Nothing reads it yet.
This file is the decision made concrete; it is not wiring.
refComment: A full 40-character SHA, deliberately. A branch name or a short SHA is a
moving or ambiguous target, and the whole value of a pin is that the proofs
CI runs are the proofs somebody read.
WHY THIS SHA AND NOT origin/main's TIP: every measurement in the KAN-518
decision was taken here. While that work was in progress origin/main advanced
one of the seven scripts swept. That commit was re-read: it adds `owner`
assertions and leaves the skip/exit shape untouched, so the sweep's verdict
holds there too. The pin still names e8729f5 because a pin should name what
was actually validated, and moving it is a reviewed act rather than a default.

detail: This pin does not expire on a date, and that is a decision rather than an
omission. A date-triggered red goes off when the calendar moves rather than
when anything drifted, and the only action it can prompt is bumping the
date — which trains a reviewer to clear the check without reading it. That
is a lying green with extra steps.
What is true instead: this pin is refreshed when somebody changes what the
imported proofs assert, and the refresh is a PR against CrabCast carrying a
re-run of the suite at the new ref. Whoever moves a crabcast-facing proof in
whoNoticesWhenItRots: ⚠ NOBODY, MECHANICALLY, AND THAT IS THE ACCEPTED COST OF THIS DECISION.
Stated plainly because Task 2 of KAN-518 permits 'nothing' as an answer only
if it is written down. Both of CrabCast's guards scope to the flat path
`scripts/verify-*.mjs`; this file is not that path, an untracked CI-time
checkout is not any path `git ls-files` returns, and neither guard audits
either. Measured, at the refs above: three real imported proofs plus their
shared library, tracked at `scripts/butchr/`, left verify-proof-registry and
verify-proof-verdicts BOTH green, both exit 0, and the registry counted the
same 84 proofs as if the four files were not there.
The same two guards go RED BY NAME on a flat unaccounted file, measured in
the same session, which is what makes the green above a reading of the world
rather than a reading of a broken search.
The honest half-cover, when KAN-519 builds it: a CrabCast-owned proof at the
flat path can audit THIS FILE — that the ref is 40 hex characters and that
the checkout CI performed is at it. That puts the PIN inside the perimeter.
It never puts the PROOFS inside it, and no placement does.
